I found no meaning drift that would mislead a learner. The meaning is faithful throughout, and the "tu" register holds ("Explore le catalogue"). The fixes are style and terminology. The product name switches between "fonctions Qiskit" and "Qiskit Functions" across [1], [3] and [4], sometimes within one paragraph. "Overhead" is rendered as "surcharge" ("surcharge de mesure", "Méthode sans surcharge"), where "surcoût" is the natural French term. "Zero Noise Extrapolation" became the odd "extrapolation du bruit zéro". [15] has several calques: "d'ordres de grandeur" is missing "plusieurs", and "Alimenté par un vote optimisé quantiquement" and "résultant en" read as English syntax.

examples.source: Introduction to Qiskit Functions

editor_note: The translation is faithful and consistently uses the informal "tu" ("Installe le client IBM Quantum Compute", "suis les instructions", "mettre fréquemment à jour tes dépendances"), and the tip block's "notes de version" and "politique de dépréciation" are correct renderings.

The translation is faithful and uses the informal "tu" consistently, but it has two small problems. In [4], "investigate abnormal activity" became "détecter les activités anormales". Detecting is a different task from investigating, which here means examining events after the fact, so this is a slight change in meaning even if it won't really mislead anyone. In the table in [10], "Déclenchée par" is fine, but "Backend" is capitalised in the first rows and lower-case in the last row ("configuration des lanes du backend"), so a native editor would make it consistent.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout: 20 questions with at least 16 correct to pass, the lock after two failed attempts, and the Credly privacy notice all match the English. examples.translation: Félicitations pour avoir terminé ce cours !
examples.suggested: Félicitations d'avoir terminé ce cours !

editor_note: The meaning holds throughout and the tu register is used consistently ("te guide", "Télécharge les diapositives"). The one slip is in the Shor tooltip in [3], where "journal paper" became "article de journal". That is a calque, because "journal" in French means a newspaper. editor_note: The meaning is accurate throughout: the 20-question exam, the 16-answer pass mark, the lock after two failed attempts and the Credly data notice all match the English. editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. editor_note: All four rewritten entries (102, 106, 108, 110) keep the English meaning, and none would mislead a learner. Entry 110 keeps every claim: Krylov starts slower than numpy's full diagonalization, becomes advantageous as the matrix grows, and still does so with a lower acceptable error, only at a larger matrix size. Two phrasings read as calques that a native editor would smooth. In 108, "Cela est fait ci-dessous" is a stiff passive. In 110, "même si l'on réduit notre erreur acceptable" mixes the impersonal "l'on" with "notre", and "Cela vaut la peine d'être décortiqué" is a literal rendering of "worth picking apart".

examples.source: This is true even if we lower our acceptable error, but the advantage sets in at a larger matrix size. This is worth picking apart.
examples.translation: Cela est vrai même si l'on réduit notre erreur acceptable, mais l'avantage apparaît à une dimension de matrice plus grande. Cela vaut la peine d'être décortiqué.
examples.suggested: C'est vrai même si l'on réduit l'erreur tolérée, mais l'avantage n'apparaît alors qu'à une dimension de matrice plus grande. Cela mérite qu'on s'y attarde.
examples.why: The meaning is correct, but 'l'on … notre' mixes two voices, 'erreur acceptable' is a calque of 'acceptable error' where French would say 'erreur tolérée' or 'tolérance', and 'vaut la peine d'être décortiqué' is a literal rendering of the idiom.

editor_note: Entry 29 is faithful. The ket/column-vector convention, the point that NumPy 1D arrays don't distinguish row from column vectors, the "no numerical effect" caveat and the Dirac-notation remark all survive without drift. Two stylistic slips remain. The closing clause "corresponde plus étroitement à la correspondance habituelle" repeats the same root and reads as a calque. The entry also switches to "nous adoptons" while the rest of the page consistently uses "on" (e.g. "on va projeter", "on peut faire").

examples.source: although `x1.T @ H @ x2` more closely matches the usual Dirac-notation correspondence
examples.translation: bien que `x1.T @ H @ x2` corresponde plus étroitement à la correspondance habituelle en notation de Dirac
examples.suggested: bien que `x1.T @ H @ x2` reflète plus fidèlement l'écriture habituelle en notation de Dirac
examples.why: The 'corresponde ... correspondance' repetition is clumsy, and 'plus étroitement' is a literal rendering of 'more closely'.

examples.source: we are implicitly adopting the common convention
examples.translation: nous adoptons implicitement la convention courante
examples.suggested: on adopte implicitement la convention courante
examples.why: The rest of the page consistently uses impersonal 'on' for the authorial we, and this entry breaks that.

editor_note: This placeholder page has three entries, and all three are faithful and natural: "Un tour d'horizon des autres cours et parcours d'apprentissage", "Continue ton parcours d'apprentissage" (informal "tu" as required) and "Leçon à venir !".

The meaning holds throughout, and the "tu" register stays consistent. In the privacy notice [12], "third-party data processor" comes out as "processeur de données tiers", a calque; the usual GDPR term in French is "sous-traitant (tiers)". Also in [12], "réclamer le badge" reads as a calque of "claim"; "récupérer" or "accepter" is more natural. In [7], "passe l'examen à IBM Training" and "Cet examen est destiné à être passé après avoir lu…" are stiff, and the infinitive clause has no clear subject.

examples.line_approx: AVIS : IBM utilise les services de Credly, un processeur de données tiers
examples.source: a third-party data processor authorized by IBM
examples.translation: un processeur de données tiers autorisé par IBM
examples.suggested: un sous-traitant tiers de traitement des données autorisé par IBM
examples.why: 'Processeur de données' is a calque. The standard French legal term (GDPR/RGPD) for a data processor is 'sous-traitant'.

examples.line_approx: avec des instructions pour réclamer le badge
examples.source: with instructions for claiming the badge
examples.translation: avec des instructions pour réclamer le badge
examples.suggested: avec des instructions pour récupérer ton badge
examples.why: 'Réclamer' suggests demanding something you are owed. French Credly/IBM wording uses 'accepter' or 'récupérer'.

examples.line_approx: passe l'examen à IBM® Training. Cet examen est destiné à être passé après avoir lu
examples.source: take the exam at IBM Training. This exam is intended to be taken after reading the lessons in this course.
examples.translation: passe l'examen à IBM® Training. Cet examen est destiné à être passé après avoir lu les leçons de ce cours.
examples.suggested: passe l'examen sur IBM® Training. Cet examen est prévu pour être passé une fois que tu as lu les leçons de ce cours.
examples.why: 'À IBM Training' is odd for an online platform, and 'être passé après avoir lu' has no clear subject for the infinitive, which is stiff translationese.

editor_note: Entry 145 keeps the meaning of the English. The negation holds ("il n'existe aucun coefficient ... pour satisfaire ces deux équations"), and the conclusion "est un état intriqué" matches the source. "Produit tensoriel d'états quantiques individuels" also quietly fixes the English singular "individual quantum state", and it uses the same wording as entry 139. The one thing a native editor would change is typographic: the English serial comma before "et" in "$a_0$, $a_1$, $b_0$, et $b_1$" was carried over, and standard French punctuation drops it.

examples.source: no coefficients $a_0$, $a_1$, $b_0$, and $b_1$ to satisfy these two equations
examples.translation: il n'existe aucun coefficient $a_0$, $a_1$, $b_0$, et $b_1$ pour satisfaire ces deux équations
examples.suggested: il n'existe aucun coefficient $a_0$, $a_1$, $b_0$ et $b_1$ qui satisfasse ces deux équations
examples.why: The serial (Oxford) comma before 'et' is copied from English, and French typography leaves it out. Using 'qui satisfasse' instead of 'pour satisfaire' would also read more idiomatically. The meaning is unaffected.

editor_note: Entry 48 is faithful and natural: "Consulte les guides et la référence API suivants" uses the informal tu register, and the link title "Configurer l'atténuation des erreurs" matches the rendering in entry 42 exactly.

The meaning is faithful and would not mislead a learner. A native editor would still fix some calqued phrasing. "Ce cours en replay d'événement" copies "event replay course" word for word, and "axées sur la construction d'un calcul" flattens "building toward", which describes the lessons working step by step toward a utility-scale calculation. "Quantum computing" is also rendered two ways on this short page: "informatique quantique" in [0] and "calcul quantique" in [4].

examples.source: This event replay course consists of 14 lessons and labs
examples.translation: Ce cours en replay d'événement comprend 14 leçons et labs
examples.suggested: Ce cours, issu de la rediffusion d'un événement, comprend 14 leçons et travaux pratiques
examples.why: 'cours en replay d'événement' copies the English noun stack word for word and is not idiomatic French.

examples.source: but they are focused on building toward a utility-scale calculation
examples.translation: mais elles sont axées sur la construction d'un calcul à l'échelle utilitaire
examples.suggested: mais elles convergent progressivement vers un calcul à l'échelle utilitaire
examples.why: 'building toward' means the course moves step by step toward the goal. 'la construction d'un calcul' is stiff and loses that sense of progression.

examples.source: important topics in quantum computing
examples.translation: sujets importants en calcul quantique
examples.suggested: sujets importants en informatique quantique
examples.why: Entry [0] renders 'quantum computing' as 'informatique quantique'. The page should use one term for it.

editor_note: Entry 100 keeps the English meaning ("Suzuki–Trotter d'ordre supérieur (quatrième ordre)", "en suivant les exemples montrés ci-dessus"), and its "du quatrième ordre" matches entries 101 and 104.

Rewritten entry 50 is faithful and idiomatic: the Lie–Trotter formula is left unchanged, and "Let us count the operations for this circuit" becomes "Comptons les opérations de ce circuit", which matches the later "compte les opérations de ce circuit" in entry 70.

The meaning holds throughout. The CVaR definition, the alpha=1/alpha=0 limits, the SAT/SWAP explanation and the max-cut eigenvalue condition all match the English, so a learner would not be misled. Several terms are rendered inconsistently. 'shots' is 'mesures' in [16] but 'tirs' in [51]. 'initial mapping' is 'mappage initial' in [15] but 'mapping initial' from [36] on. CVaR is spelled out as 'valeur conditionnelle à risque' in [16] but left in English in [49]. [33] slips into the formal 'convertissez', and [16] has two small wording problems: the calque 'valeurs objectives' and 'averaging' flattened into 'lissage'.

examples.source: First, map the problem onto a quantum circuit that is suited for the QAOA.
examples.translation: Tout d'abord, convertissez le problème en un circuit quantique adapté au QAOA.
examples.suggested: Tout d'abord, convertis le problème en un circuit quantique adapté au QAOA.
examples.why: The rest of the page uses 'tu', so the formal 'vous' form is a register slip.

examples.source: we determine $\alpha$ and the number of shots
examples.translation: nous déterminons $\alpha$ et le nombre de tirs
examples.suggested: Pick one rendering of 'shots' and use it everywhere (e.g. 'tirs' or 'shots'); [16] uses 'mesures'.
examples.why: 'shots' is rendered as 'mesures' in [16] and 'tirs' here, so the same concept goes by two names on one page.

examples.source: SWAP strategy with SAT initial mapping
examples.translation: Stratégie SWAP avec mappage initial SAT
examples.suggested: Stratégie SWAP avec mapping initial SAT (to match [36]-[44])
examples.why: 'mappage' here but 'mapping' in [36], [37], [40], [42] and [44]: an inconsistency within the file.

examples.source: objective values ... while still applying some averaging to smooth out the optimization landscape
examples.translation: valeurs objectives ... l'application d'un certain lissage pour régulariser le paysage d'optimisation
examples.suggested: valeurs de la fonction objectif ... tout en conservant une certaine moyenne pour lisser le paysage d'optimisation
examples.why: 'valeurs objectives' is a calque (it should be 'valeurs de la fonction objectif'), and replacing 'averaging' with 'lissage' blurs the point that the smoothing comes from averaging.

examples.source: define a Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) cost function
examples.translation: définir une fonction de coût Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR)
examples.suggested: définir une fonction de coût de valeur conditionnelle à risque (CVaR)
examples.why: [16] already translates the term as 'valeur conditionnelle à risque', so leaving it in English here is inconsistent.

editor_note: None of the 10 rewritten entries changes the meaning. Entries 78 and 82 now translate "expectation value" as "valeurs moyennes". That is the right French term, but the rest of the page (16, 25, 81, 85, 88) still says "valeurs attendues", so the concept is now split within the file. In entry 82, "meilleure extrapolation heuristique" moves the adverb: the English says the extrapolation was chosen as best by a heuristic, not that it is the best heuristic extrapolation. Entry 74 says "portes ... twirlées" where entry 49 says "couches soumises au twirling", a small style mismatch.

examples.source: You fetch the raw and mitigated expectation values
examples.translation: Tu récupères les valeurs moyennes brutes et atténuées
examples.suggested: Keep "valeurs moyennes" and align entries 16, 25, 81, 85 and 88, which still use "valeurs attendues"
examples.why: Entries 78 and 82 now use "valeurs moyennes", which is correct, but the untouched entries still use the calque "valeurs attendues", so the page uses two terms for one concept.

examples.source: (based on heuristically best extrapolation)
examples.translation: (basées sur la meilleure extrapolation heuristique)
examples.suggested: (basées sur l'extrapolation jugée la meilleure de manière heuristique)
examples.why: The adverb "heuristically" becomes an adjective on "extrapolation", which slightly changes what is being called heuristic.

examples.source: layers of twirled two-qubit basis gates
examples.translation: couches de portes de base à deux qubits twirlées
examples.suggested: couches de portes de base à deux qubits soumises au twirling
examples.why: The hybrid "twirlées" is stiff and does not match "soumises au twirling" in entry 49.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout. The caveats about methodology versus drift in [28], [79], [80], [87] and [88] are kept intact, including the 53/56/142 µs medians and the above/below directions. The key verb 'refresh' is translated two ways: 'actualiser/actualisées' in [0], [8], [11] and [27], but 'rafraîchi(es)' in [88], [90], [92] and [94]. 'workflow' is also split between 'flux de travail' (most entries) and the bare English 'workflow' in [77] and [92]. There are some small fluency slips: [92] 'rafraîchis les propriétés proche du moment où' is ungrammatical, [5] 'Résultats d'apprentissage' is a calque, and [24] 'est démontrée' is a calque. The step headings also switch from infinitives ([46], [56]) to a noun form in [63].

examples.source: refresh the properties close to the time you actually execute your workload
examples.translation: rafraîchis les propriétés proche du moment où tu exécutes réellement ta charge de travail
examples.suggested: actualise les propriétés peu avant d'exécuter réellement ta charge de travail
examples.why: 'proche du moment' used adverbially is ungrammatical; it also uses 'rafraîchir' where the rest of the page uses 'actualiser'.

examples.source: The refreshed values are a self-consistent snapshot
examples.translation: Les valeurs rafraîchies sont un instantané autocohérent
examples.suggested: Les valeurs actualisées sont un instantané autocohérent
examples.why: The title and [27] use 'actualiser/actualisées'; switching to 'rafraîchi' in [88]-[94] is inconsistent within the file.

examples.source: the drift this workflow is designed to catch
examples.translation: la dérive que ce workflow est conçu pour détecter
examples.suggested: la dérive que ce flux de travail est conçu pour détecter
examples.why: Everywhere else the page says 'flux de travail'; [77] and [92] fall back to the English 'workflow'.

examples.source: Learning outcomes
examples.translation: Résultats d'apprentissage
examples.suggested: Objectifs d'apprentissage
examples.why: 'Résultats d'apprentissage' is a calque; French teaching material normally says 'Objectifs d'apprentissage'.

examples.source: a multi-echo (CPMG-style) variant is demonstrated at the end of this tutorial
examples.translation: une variante multi-écho (de type CPMG) est démontrée à la fin de ce tutoriel
examples.suggested: une variante multi-écho (de type CPMG) est présentée à la fin de ce tutoriel
examples.why: In French, 'démontrer' means to prove. Showing a variant is 'présenter' or 'illustrer'.
